expectations.text: Recommends keeping calculatePrice as its own file (rejects inlining it into the component)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Don't inline it' and 'Keep calculatePrice.ts separate.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the abstraction-over-file-structure heuristic (clean typed interface, hides implementation)
expectations.evidence: 'Fully typed inputs and outputs. The signature is the contract. Anyone — human or AI — can understand what goes in and what comes out without reading the body.' and 'a pure, typed, tested, 6-times-reused function is one of the highest-leverage abstractions you can have.'

expectations.text: Notes the agent uses the typed call site without needing the internals (understood in isolation)
expectations.evidence: 'A typed import like import { calculatePrice } from ... is a clear, greppable signpost.' and 'The signature is the contract. Anyone — human or AI — can understand what goes in and what comes out without reading the body.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 'inline so Claude sees it all' argument for a clean, reused, tested abstraction
expectations.evidence: 'The AI argument doesn't survive scrutiny... "One place" is a context-window heuristic from a bygone era. Modern agents navigate multi-file codebases routinely.' and 'The "see it all in one place" benefit is illusory — agents follow imports fine.'
